title: Preparing for a job interview
text:
A job interview can be stressful, but good preparation makes a huge difference. Employers often say that they can tell within the first few minutes whether a candidate has prepared properly. The following steps will help you feel more confident and make a strong impression.

Research the company
Start by learning as much as you can about the organisation. Read its website, especially the sections about its mission, products and recent news. Look at its social media and, if possible, find out what current or former employees say about working there. You do not need to memorise facts, but you should be able to explain why you want to work for this company in particular, not just any company.

Study the job description
Print the advertisement and underline the key skills and responsibilities. For each one, think of a specific example from your experience that shows you have that skill. Interviewers increasingly ask behavioural questions, such as "Tell me about a time when you had to meet a difficult deadline." A useful way to answer is the STAR method: describe the Situation, the Task, the Action you took and the Result.

Prepare your own questions
At the end of most interviews, you will be asked if you have any questions. Saying "No, thank you" can suggest a lack of interest. Prepare two or three thoughtful questions about the team, the training opportunities or the challenges of the role. Avoid asking about salary and holidays in the first interview unless the interviewer raises the topic.

Plan the practical details
Check the time, the place and the name of the person who will interview you. If the interview is in person, plan your journey and aim to arrive about ten minutes early – not much earlier, as this can be inconvenient for the employer. If it is online, test your camera, microphone and internet connection the day before, and choose a quiet place with a neutral background.

On the day
Dress slightly more formally than people usually do in that workplace. Bring copies of your CV and a notebook. Listen carefully to each question, and do not be afraid to take a moment to think before you answer. Be honest: if you do not know something, say so, and explain how you would find out.

After the interview
Within twenty-four hours, send a short email thanking the interviewer for their time. It is a simple gesture, but surprisingly few candidates do it, and it can help you stand out.
